text.p: The chairman of a special committee of Loctite Corp. and a representative of Dillon Read met this week with the chief executive officer of a potential bidder, Loctite disclosed Tuesday in a regulatory document.

However, the bidder was not Henkel KGaA, the German company that has launched a hostile takeover attempt for the maker of adhesives and speciality chemicals, Loctite said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
It said that Robert Fiondella, chairman of the special committee, met with a potential bidder on Monday, but it did not name the bidder.
Early last month Henkel, a German chemicals and consumer products group, made a $2.1 billion, or $57.75 per share, bid for the 65 percent of Loctite that it does not already own.
Fiondella and the Dillon Read representative discussed certain terms of a possible transaction with the potential bidder, the filing said.
Also, advisers to the special committee are holding talks with the potential bidder's advisers regarding the terms of a merger agreement, the filing said.

However, Fiondella said "there can be no assurance that this potential bidder will submit an acquitision proposal or that the special committee will recommend or that the board of directors will approve any such proposal."
Late last month, Hartford, Conn.-based Loctite offered to sell itself to the highest bidder, but analysts said at the time it was unlikely that it would find an alternative to Henkel's offer.
Loctite set a Dec. 4 deadline for presenting new bids.

About 10 top U.S. and European companies have been mentioned as potential Henkel rivals, but sources said those companies have avoided or outright refused to take the role of white knight because of Henkel's major Loctite ownership and board presence.
Among the companies, DuPont Co., Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co. and Ashland Inc. were said to have been approached by Loctite. Officials of those companies have declined to comment.

Early in November, German-based Henkel raised its bid for the remaining portion of Loctite to $57.75 a share from $56, and turned its takeover proposal into a hostile tender offer. Loctite rejected the offer as insufficient.
Loctite stock was up $1.125 at $60.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
